name: multiple_choice: Imagine that you are a consulting data scientist for…

request.questionText: Imagine that you are a consulting data scientist for a candidate in the 2024 presidential election, working with data on political and economic metrics. You fit a linear model regressing presidential approval rates (percentage from Gallup polls) on the following predictors: cpi -- Consumer Price Index gasprice -- average gas price (dollars) sp500 -- S&P 500 index unemploy -- unemployment rate (percent) You use the model results to produce standardized estimates and intervals: Parameter | Std. Coef. | 95% CI ----------------------------------------- (Intercept) | 0.00000001 | [-0.11, 0.11] gasprice | -0.43 | [-0.72, -0.14] unemploy | 0.05 | [-0.13, 0.23] cpi | -0.40 | [-0.69, -0.11] sp500 | -0.06 | [-0.27, 0.15] Which of the following statements is accurate with respect to these model results? Holding constant other model predictors: (1) a 1% increase in unemployment is associated with an increase in approval rates of 0.05 standard deviations. (2) a one-standard deviation increase in the Consumer Price Index (cpi) is associated with a decrease in approval rates not exceeding 69%, with 95% confidence. (3) a one-standard-deviation increase in gas price is associated with a minimum decrease in approval rates of 0.14 standard deviations, with 95% confidence.
